title: Belfast Is Burning. India's Cricket Tour of Ireland May Be the Next Casualty.
excerpt: Anti-immigration riots in Northern Ireland have put India's two-match T20I series in doubt. The BCCI is monitoring the situation, and a venue change is on the table.
body:
India's scheduled two-match T20I series against Ireland, set to begin on June 26 at Belfast's Stormont Cricket Ground, is now in serious doubt after anti-immigration violence convulsed Northern Ireland this week.

The riots were triggered by a knife attack in which a 30-year-old Sudanese asylum seeker injured and blinded a local man. What began as peaceful protests against immigration policy rapidly descended into arson, looting, and targeted attacks on minority communities. Protesters have burned cars, trucks, and shops near Belfast city centre. Police deployed water cannons. At least 16 people have been arrested and 12 police officers injured.

## The Cricketing Fallout

Cricket Ireland issued a statement acknowledging the crisis: "Cricket Ireland is continuing to monitor the situation in areas currently experiencing community unrest and will make a decision within the next 48 hours regarding this Sunday's Irish Senior Cup and National Cup fixtures."

The board added: "The safety and security of players, coaches, match officials, and supporters is paramount in our deliberations."

The Board of Control for Cricket in India has been in direct contact with Cricket Ireland. According to Dainik Jagran, BCCI officials are "monitoring the situation" and have made clear that a venue change is a real possibility if normalcy is not restored before the Indian squad's arrival.

A BCCI source told the newspaper that "the safety of the players and the members of the coaching staff is paramount," but emphasised that any venue shift would be Cricket Ireland's call.

The two T20Is on June 26 and 28 were meant to be a warm-up before India's marquee white-ball tour of England — five T20Is and three ODIs in July. Moving the games to Dublin's Malahide Cricket Club, which hosted all seven India-Ireland matches between 2007 and 2023, is the most likely fallback.

## Indians in Belfast Are on Edge

The violence has rattled Northern Ireland's small but growing Indian community. While the protests are not specifically targeting South Asians, the broader anti-immigrant sentiment has made minority residents anxious. Indians in Belfast have been subjected to racist attacks in the past, and the current atmosphere has heightened those fears.

Reuters reported that Ruchira Rangaprasad, an Indian woman who moved to Northern Ireland three years ago, began posting on social media that she would cook meals for families too afraid to leave their homes. More than 30 volunteers — most of them strangers — stepped forward to help distribute food boxes.

"People are scared to step out of their home, and food is like a basic need," she told Reuters. "So that's why I thought, let me cook and help feed people."

Northern Ireland is 97 per cent white, according to its most recent census. The influx of asylum seekers and immigrants in recent years has generated friction in a society still scarred by its own sectarian history.

## What Happens Next

Cricket Ireland has promised further updates as the situation develops. The latest reports suggest that the violence has begun to ease, with a heavy police presence helping to stabilise the worst-affected areas. But the situation remains volatile, and the BCCI is unlikely to take risks with its players' safety.

For India's cricket board, the stakes are primarily logistical. For Cricket Ireland, they are existential. Hosting India is the single most commercially important fixture on Ireland's cricketing calendar. Losing it — or moving it to a different city — would be a significant financial and reputational blow.

The Indian squad, fresh from an ODI series, is expected to be announced in full within the week. Whether they board a plane to Belfast or Dublin will depend on what happens on Belfast's streets in the next ten days.

*Sources: Cricket Ireland; BCCI via Dainik Jagran; Reuters; Sportskeeda; Inside Sport India*
nri_angle: Indians living in Belfast are anxious as anti-immigration riots grip the city — and the scheduled India cricket tour to Stormont could be relocated, depriving the local diaspora of a rare opportunity to watch the national team play.
author: Diaspora Desk
